Definition
Digital circuits are not completely new circuits. They are made from many of the same components used in analog circuits.
INTRODUCTIONM
The difference between digital and analog circuits is the way we look at the inputs and outputs.
A lamp in an analog circuit is OFF, dimly lit, brightly lit or somewhere in between.
A lamp in a digital circuit is either ON or OFF. The amount of brightness doesn't matter.
For the digital circuit to operate properly the two states of ON or OFF must be defined clearly.
Let's begin the lesson on BUFFERS AND INVERTERS...........................
LESSON MENU
BUFFERS AND INVERTERS
Buffers and inverters are digital circuits that have one input and one output.
DISCUSSION
Let's discuss the buffer's operation first.
The buffer differs from the AND, OR and NOT functions in that a HIGH input always produces a HIGH output.
A LOW input always produces a LOW output.
The truth table for the buffer is very simple to make.
Fill in the missing value in the buffer's truth table.eric answer (25k).................ble.le.
Remember, whatever logic level comes into a buffer, the same logic level will leave the buffer.

The buffer performs three basic functions in digital circuits:
PROTECTION - The buffer is used to protect digital components from an input voltage or current that is too high.
For example, the input to the buffer is 10 volts. The digital circuit is designed to operate at 5 volts or less.
The 10 volts applied to the buffer gates the lower 4 volts through to the digital circuit.
DRIVER - The buffer is also used as a driver circuit when several digital circuits operate from the same voltage source.
In this example, the same 5 volts is needed to drive each of the three digital circuits.
Each circuit adds a load to the 5 volts until the effective voltage is too small to operate any of the circuits.
The buffer is able to maintain current at a high enough level so that voltage is not loaded down.
SWITCH - The buffer is also used as a switch. It functions much like an amplifier, but is only capable of producing two different output states.
For example, this digital circuit must sound a burglar alarm in the event of a break in.
The actual output voltage from the digital circuit is only 5 volts; 10 volts is needed to operate the alarm.rm.
The buffer is used to gate through a voltage large enough to drive the alarm.

Now, let's discuss the Inverter............................
The inverter is a combination of the buffer and NOT function. A HIGH input is LOW at the output and a LOW input is HIGH at the output.
When the NOT function is used with other digital circuits, the NOT function is represented with a circle, commonly referred to a BUBBLE.
The inverter is used to change the output of a digital circuit to the opposite condition of the input.
Schematically, inverters can be drawn with the bubble on the input. The gate will functionally operate the same.

THRESHOLD VOLTAGESE

While we commonly think of logic highs & lows as 0 volts and 5 volts, there is an acceptable voltage range. The range is stipulated by the manufacturer and defines what is considered a logic high or low..w.
DISCUSSION
Let's examine the ranges for a 5 volt system using standard TTL logic.
When TTL was devised, it was agreed upon by industry that logic LOW's would be defined as any voltage level .8 volts or less and logic HIGH's as 2 volts or more.
There's actually some degree of variance involved based on whether we are looking at an input or output.
These are the manufacturer's guaranteed voltages. Notice that the output voltages have stiffer mandatory levels. to determine proper operation.
This ensures that TTL outputs will always meet the minimum and maximum input requirements of another TTL gate.
The voltages between .8 volts and 2 volts are considered indeterminate and illegal in as much as they are not valid logic levels...........................................
Indeed, when troubleshooting a TTL circuit and a voltage is measured that's between .8 and 2 V, it is often called a "float" and points to a likely open in the circuit.
The actual point where a TTL device switches from a low to a high or a high to a low is normally at roughly 1.4 volts, but to build in a margin of error, the .8 and 2V levels were established.
One of the reasons for the broad range between the valid logic HIGH and the valid logic LOW, is the effect of noise on logic levels..
If we assume that switching indeed occurs at 1.4V and measured LOW/HIGH levels were at 1.0 V/1.6 V, a positive going noise spike of only 600 mV could drive a low to a high.
A full discussion of noise effects on logic circuits is discussed in the Logic Families lesson.
